result:
The proposed answer matches what the problem most plausibly intends, but the "if and only if" step is not proved in general.

**What holds.** Since $r\ge 1$, write $V^*=(V^*)^G\oplus W$ with $W^G=0$. Then
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(R,t)=\frac{1}{(1-t)^r}\operatorname{Hilb}(k[W]^G,t).$$
Each group element fixes $(V^*)^G$ pointwise. So any eigenspace of an element for an eigenvalue $\zeta\ne1$ lies in $W$, which has dimension $d-r$. Hence the pole at any root of unity $\zeta\ne1$ has order at most $d-r$.

A pole of order $m$ at $\zeta$ contributes only to $a_i(n)$ with $i\le m-1\le d-r-1$. So $a_i$ is constant for all $i\ge d-r$, which gives $r$ constant coefficients.

**The gap.** Non-constancy of $a_i$ for every $i<d-r$ is not shown. A pole of order exactly $d-r$ at some $\zeta\ne1$ is needed, and it can fail. For example, take $\mathbb Z/3$ acting by $(1,\omega,\omega^{-1})$ on $k^3$. The poles at $\omega^{\pm1}$ have order 1, not $d-r=2$, so $a_1$ is constant even though $1<d-r$. For this reason the answer depends on $G$ unless the problem intends the generic statement that exactly the top $r$ coefficients $a_{d-r},\dots,a_{d-1}$ are constant. Under that intended statement the sum is
$$\sum_{i=d-r}^{d-1} i=\frac{r(2d-r-1)}{2}.$$

The trivial-group case ($r=d$) gives $d(d-1)/2$, which agrees with the formula. I could not confirm the intended statement against a source.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
